$comment: M13. A search page: how he went through the place (the first paragraph, which the first find joins), the body the engine writes (the finds, the things left alone, what they are worth), and a last word before any decision or next lead. Holes: act (how he went through it, off search-act, or the one thing he searched; bind prop for a thing the act card names, 'the one good chair'), left (bind prop: the first thing in the room besides what he started with, which the page names after the first find and says he went through with the rest — a search takes the whole room), body. Card holes: prop (place-ambient: bind prop; the room's texture, said in the first paragraph). Slots: {place} {Place} {victim} {hour} {object} (the thing searched, when it was one); roles {prop}. Every part is said in the first paragraph, before the first find, wherever it sits round the body. A later bind of prop wins over an earlier one, so a sheet that binds both left and act puts left first: the act card's thing when it offers one (with its own pay line), else the other thing in the room. Never a verdict: a last word is about the room, the search, the detective — never what a find means.

sheets.name: The way through
sheets.notes: The way through, and a last word on a thing the act card named (the kitchen end, the one good chair: its own pay line) or, when the card offers none, on the first other thing in the room he went through.

callback: I put {prop} back where I found it, when I had been through it with the rest.
I went through {prop} last, on the way out. Some things you save for when you know what to ask them.
I put {prop} back where it stood. I’d know where to find it, which is more than I can say for my hat most mornings.
plain: I put the room back roughly the way I found it. Roughly is the best anybody does.
I dusted off my knees and let myself out. The room didn’t see me to the door.
I made sure I hadn’t left my hat behind. It’s happened.
I went out the way I came in, only dustier.

sheets.name: The room first
sheets.notes: The room's texture before he touches anything (a place-ambient card, said in the first paragraph), then the way through; the last word brings the room's thing back.

parts.text: I gave the place a minute to get used to me.
alt: I let the place get a look at me first.
Before I touched anything, I just looked.
I didn’t touch anything at first. Looking breaks less.

callback: By the time I was done, I knew {prop} better than I wanted to.
I left {prop} the way I found it. It was the one thing in the place I was sure I hadn’t moved.
I said goodnight to {prop} on the way out. We’d been through a lot together.
plain: The place looked no different when I’d finished. I couldn’t say the same for me.
I dusted my hands off on my coat. The coat has seen worse.
It took longer than it looked. Rooms always do.
When I was done, the place went quiet again, as if it had been holding its breath.

sheets.name: One thing, properly
sheets.notes: A search of one thing: a join that says so, the thing, and a last word that puts it back (or on the other thing he went through after it). A search of one thing is still a search of the room: it starts there.

parts.text: I started with one thing and took my time over it, and then I went through the rest of {place}.
alt: I gave one thing all my attention first, and the rest of {place} what was left.
One thing first, properly, and then the whole of {place} after it. I’d rather do one thing properly than everything badly.
I had one thing in mind, and I went through it properly before I did the rest of {place}.

callback: I got to {prop} after {object}. I only have the two hands, and I’d been using both on {object}.
{Prop} got what was left of me after {object}. I’d given {object} the best of it.
I got round to {prop} last. One thing at a time is about my speed.
plain: I put {object} back the way it had been, near enough. Near enough is what I get paid for.
I gave {object} one last look, to be polite, and put everything back.
That was {object}, gone over properly, and the rest of the place after it.
I straightened up slowly. Going over one thing properly is hard on the back.

sheets.name: A good haul
sheets.notes: A search that turned up three things or more: the last word is about having his hands full, never about what the finds mean.

callback: My hands were full already by the time I got to {prop}.
I went through {prop} too, and could have used another pair of hands for it.
{Prop} got its turn as well. I was carrying about as much as one notebook can hold.
plain: That was more than a room usually gives me. I wrote it all down before it could change its mind.
The room had been generous. I wrote fast, in case it wanted anything back.
I hadn’t found this much in one place since I last cleaned out my own coat.
I stood up with a full page and sore knees, which is as good as the job gets.

sheets.name: Down on the floor
sheets.notes: Plain: the search, and a last word on the detective's knees and back. No role, so it is a sheet for a page without a callback.

plain: I got up off the floor in two stages. My knees wanted it known that neither one was their idea.
Somewhere in there my back had stopped speaking to me. I couldn’t say I blamed it.
I stayed down there a moment longer than I needed to. Getting up is the hard part.
My hat had rolled under something while I wasn’t looking. The room had been searching me back.

sheets.name: Not much
sheets.notes: A search that turned up one thing or nothing: a last word on the time it took.

plain: It wasn’t much for the time it took. Rooms don’t pay by the hour.
I had been more thorough than the room deserved, and it paid me about what it thought I was worth.
That was the search: short on finds and long on dust.
I’d been over every inch of it. Some of the inches twice.
